sections.h2: What the Webster County PVA decides
sections.html:
Webster County's Property Valuation Administrator, an elected official, assesses all real and personal property in the county at fair market value. The PVA's office does not decide your bill. A bill has two ingredients, the assessed value from the PVA and the rate, which comes from the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and taxing districts such as the library board and health board.

Some property is valued in Frankfort, among it public service companies and bank shares, and vehicles go in that group too. The PVA may still change a vehicle's value for high mileage or a body shop's estimate.

The PVA's counter is on the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Phone 270-639-7016, Monday through Friday, 8 to 4. The Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, shares the courthouse address, and its website carries a Property Taxes page for bill details.

sections.h2: When is the Webster County bill due?
sections.html:
The usual statewide timetable of KRS 134.015 applies. If bills were mailed late, the Department of Revenue can run an alternative schedule, so rely on the dates printed on your own bill. The Sheriff stays the place to pay until April 15.

Webster County payment stages for a real estate bill
Payment windowAmount owed
Through November 1Printed amount minus 2 percent
November 2 to year endPrinted amount
JanuaryPrinted amount plus 5 percent
February through April 15Printed amount plus 10 percent

After April 15, any open bill moves to the County Clerk, with a recorded lien and added fees. For a payoff after that date, call the Clerk's office at 270-639-7006.

sections.h2: How fast does a late Webster County bill grow?
sections.html:
Fast. Once the Clerk's office takes over a delinquent real estate bill, charges pile on in layers. At the handoff from the Sheriff, the bill already includes the 10 percent penalty and the Sheriff's add-on. Pay within five business days and only a modest extra cost applies. After the county attorney sends a first notice, the total jumps again, and interest of 1 percent runs each month. Commissions follow, and a newspaper advertisement in June adds more.

The sale falls between 90 and 135 days after the handoff. The purchaser inherits the lien and may add its own charges, so the amount you owe is highest if a third party buys the certificate. Paying the Sheriff before April 15 avoids every one of these steps.

sections.h2: How to contest a Webster County value
sections.html:
Sit down with the PVA or a deputy first. The state will not hear an appeal from an owner who skipped that meeting. The appeal itself is filed at the County Clerk's office by close of business the next workday after inspection ends. The board wants documents: building and land details, insurance, construction costs, comparable listings.

  • The roll is displayed for 13 days beginning on the first Monday of May.
  • The board convenes roughly a month after display ends.
  • Taxpayers may make their own audio recording of the hearing.

A late-printed bill uses the value you claimed, with a supplemental bill following if the board sets a higher one. Paid agents must qualify under state rules and carry written authority.

Claim it at the PVA if you live in the home and are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement plan. The deduction is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. The state rate is 10.6 cents per $100 for 2025, with county, city, school, and district rates on top.

Disability claims need payments for the entire assessment period and a new application each year, unless the owner has a service-connected disability or a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems. After a sale, let the PVA know so the exemption leaves the old parcel.

sections.h2: Can I list a Webster County house with taxes behind?
sections.html:
Yes, though the debt does not vanish at closing. It belongs to the owner from the assessment date (KRS 134.015), and the lien outlives a sale for up to 11 years (KRS 134.420). Get written payoffs before accepting an offer: the Sheriff for this year, the Clerk for earlier ones.

The Clerk's site includes a delinquent tax lookup beside the land records. Should your certificate have been sold at the sale, the payoff goes to the buyer and includes that buyer's fees, so ask who holds it.

The sales contract normally divides the current year's bill by days of ownership. Make sure the split is written down and appears on the closing statement.

A cash buyer can take a house with open taxes as-is and clear the lien from your proceeds at closing. That path suits an inherited home, a house needing repairs, or one where a bill has already reached the Clerk, since it saves you from paying out of pocket before you sell.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list
sections.html:
Begin with the PVA at 270-639-7016. Ask what the parcel is assessed at and whether a homestead exemption is on it. Then stop at the Sheriff's Office, 270-639-5067, for this year's balance and confirm whether the bill is paid. If any earlier year went unpaid, the Clerk at 270-639-7006 can give you a payoff.

Write each figure down along with the date you were quoted. Hand the list to your closing agent so the settlement statement matches. If you plan to challenge a value, remember the appeal window is short: it opens the first Monday in May and ends the workday after the 13-day display. Missing it means living with the number until next year.

Buyers and their lenders will order a title search, and an old delinquency will turn up there. It is far easier to clear it before an offer than to renegotiate in the middle of a contract.

Webster County has 12,929 residents as of 2025, a 0.7 percent drop from 2020. Dixon holds the courthouse, and Providence is the largest of six cities that also include Clay, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft. The county runs on Central time.

There are 5,772 housing units and 4,923 households. Owner-occupied homes make up 73.8 percent of the stock, valued at a median $112,900. Owners pay a median $1,241 monthly with a mortgage and $405 without, and renters pay a median $783. Only five building permits were issued in 2025, so houses change hands mostly as resales. Providence and Sebree voted to allow alcohol sales in 2018, and Clay followed in 2022.

faqs.q: What are the Webster County PVA's address and hours?
faqs.a: On the courthouse's first floor, 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon. Call 270-639-7016 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the Webster County PVA decide my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The fiscal court, city governments, school board, and districts such as the library and health boards set rates. The PVA only determines assessed value.

faqs.q: By when must a Webster County appeal reach the County Clerk?
faqs.a: Before closing time on the workday after the 13-day roll inspection ends, and only once you have met with the PVA.

faqs.q: How much does the exemption lower a Webster County assessment?
faqs.a: It removes $49,100 from the assessed value of your own home in 2025 and 2026, if you are 65 or older or totally disabled. The PVA handles the application.

faqs.q: Why does a Webster County bill cost more at the Clerk?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty and Sheriff's add-on are included at the handoff, then 1 percent monthly interest and commissions follow. The county attorney's notice adds more.
